stories.headline: Meituan open-sources LongCat-2.0, a 1.6T coding model trained entirely on Chinese chips

key_facts.fact: Meituan officially released and open-sourced LongCat-2.0 on Tuesday, June 30, under a permissive MIT license, distributed via GitHub, Hugging Face and its native platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan officially unveiled LongCat-2.0 on GitHub, Hugging Face and its native platform... brings a native 1-million-token context window to the public domain under a highly permissive, enterprise grade, commercially viable MIT license.

key_facts.fact: LongCat-2.0 is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, dynamically activating roughly 48 billion per token, with a native 1-million-token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan has released what it claims is the country's first trillion-parameter artificial intelligence model trained entirely on home-grown hardware... LongCat-2.0, a new large language model boasting 1.6 trillion parameters and a context window of 1 million tokens.

key_facts.fact: It is the first trillion-parameter model fully pre-trained and run on a cluster of more than 50,000 domestically made Chinese ASICs, without Nvidia GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: LongCat-2.0 is the industry's first AI model with more than a trillion parameters to be fully trained and run on a cluster of 50,000 domestically made chips, Meituan said. It did not disclose which Chinese chipmaker's products were used.

key_facts.fact: Meituan says LongCat-2.0's performance is comparable to Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, released in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan says the performance of its new large language model, LongCat-2.0, is comparable to Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, which was released in February.

key_facts.fact: LongCat-2.0 was the previously anonymous stealth model 'Owl Alpha' that topped global developer charts on OpenRouter for the past two months.
key_facts.excerpt: unmasking the model as the computational engine behind 'Owl Alpha,' the anonymous stealth model that has spent the last two months commanding global developer charts on OpenRouter.

stories.headline: California signs first-of-its-kind deal to bring Claude to all state agencies at 50% off

key_facts.fact: Governor Gavin Newsom announced on June 29 a first-of-its-kind partnership letting all California state agencies access Anthropic's Claude at a 50% discounted price, with the same offer extended to cities and counties.
key_facts.excerpt: Through the agreement, state agencies may access Anthropic's AI productivity assistant, Claude, at a 50% discounted price... The agreement also provides the same discounted offer for California's local governments, including cities and counties.

key_facts.fact: The deal includes free workforce training plus technical assistance and workflow input from Anthropic developers, and makes Claude the first AI productivity tool available to all state agencies via the Department of Technology's new SITeS portal.
key_facts.excerpt: coupled with free workforce training as well as expert GenAI technical assistance and workflow input from Anthropic developers... Claude is the first AI productivity tool that will be available to all State agencies though the California Department of Technology's new Statewide Information Technology Shared Services (SITeS) portal.

key_facts.fact: California already uses Claude in several departments: CalOES and CDT for cyber defense (scanning and patching state code), the DMV to cut customer wait times, and the Department of Healthcare Services, the largest Medicaid agency in the country, for internal workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: CDT and CalOES are partnering to use Claude for cyber defense... CA DMV is using Claude to improve customer service and lower wait times, and CA Dept of Healthcare Services, the largest Medicaid Agency in the country, is using Claude for internal workflows.

key_facts.fact: Departments will pay to use Claude individually with no statewide budget allocation, and no department had started using it under the new contract as of the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: departments will pay to use Claude individually and there is not a statewide budget allocation for this technology. She added that as of now, no departments have started using the technology under the newly announced contract.

key_facts.fact: The state deal contrasts with the federal posture: the Pentagon recently declared Anthropic a 'supply-chain risk' and signed with OpenAI after Anthropic sought carve-outs against surveillance and autonomous weapons.
key_facts.excerpt: the federal government has made an enemy out of the OpenAI rival... the agency signed a deal with OpenAI instead. The government went as far as to declare Anthropic a 'supply-chain risk,' preventing the company from working with any other Pentagon contractors.

stories.headline: Amazon weighs OpenAI and own Nova models as Anthropic shifts to costlier token pricing

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on June 29 that Amazon is exploring OpenAI and its own Nova models after a renegotiated Anthropic contract shifts billing to per-token pricing next year, which could sharply raise Amazon's AI costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon is looking for cheaper alternatives to Anthropic's Claude models after a renegotiated contract will shift to token-based pricing that could substantially increase the company's AI costs, according to The Information... Amazon is already exploring options including OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's reliance on Claude runs deep, powering its Kiro coding agent, its Quick workplace assistant and Alexa for Shopping.
key_facts.excerpt: Its coding agent Kiro, workplace assistant Quick, and consumer-facing Alexa for Shopping all rely on Anthropic's models, according to The Information. A shift to token-based billing would make that dependence far more expensive.

key_facts.fact: Some Amazon engineers are already distilling Anthropic models into smaller, cheaper internal versions; Amazon holds certain rights to do so, similar to Apple's arrangement with Google Gemini.
key_facts.excerpt: some Amazon engineers are already distilling Anthropic models to build smaller, cheaper versions for internal use... Amazon has certain rights to use Anthropic's models for this purpose, according to a person familiar with the matter, similar to Apple's arrangement with Google Gemini.

key_facts.fact: Amazon disputed the report, saying the expanded partnership won't raise costs, while Anthropic said its per-token price keeps falling and called Amazon one of its most important partners.
key_facts.excerpt: An Amazon spokesperson pushed back, saying the changes from the expanded partnership won't raise costs. Anthropic points to lower prices relative to the performance its models deliver.

key_facts.fact: The strain follows large cross-investments: Amazon committed up to $50 billion to OpenAI this year and has invested a potential $33 billion in Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year Amazon committed $50 billion to OpenAI... That deal followed Amazon's initial $4 billion investment in Anthropic, which has since grown to a potential $33 billion.

stories.headline: Chamath Palihapitiya raises $135M Series A for AI coding startup 8090, takes CEO role

key_facts.fact: Chamath Palihapitiya announced on Monday, June 29 that his AI coding startup 8090 closed a $135 million Series A led by Salesforce Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, 8090 Labs, closed a $135 million round led by Salesforce Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The round also drew Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, David Sacks' Craft Ventures, David Friedberg's The Production Board and Jason Calacanis' Launch, plus angels including Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora and Quora CEO Adam D'Angelo.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo; David Sacks' Craft Ventures; fellow All-In hosts and 'besties' David Friedberg (The Production Board) and Jason Calacanis (Launch); and angel investors like Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora and Quora CEO Adam D'Angelo.

key_facts.fact: Palihapitiya said he will lead 8090 as CEO rather than serving on the board, his first full-time operating role since leaving Facebook.
key_facts.excerpt: Palihapitiya also announced on X that he will lead the startup as CEO, rather than just serving as a board member... 'Since I left Facebook, I was waiting for a moment like this to return to a full-time operating role.'

key_facts.fact: Founded in January 2024, 8090's flagship product 'Software Factory' helps corporate coders build production-quality software with enterprise controls like audit trails.
key_facts.excerpt: Palihapitiya founded 8090 Labs in January 2024 to offer an AI coding agent specifically for corporate programming teams. Its product, Software Factory, helps corporate coders use AI to build production-quality software, not just vibe-coded prototypes, with all the controls enterprises need, such as audit trails.

key_facts.fact: 8090 targets heavily regulated sectors, listing customers in healthcare, insurance, life sciences, aerospace, energy, manufacturing, financial services and the U.S. government.
key_facts.excerpt: 8090 works with the biggest, hardest, most demanding customers in the most regulated industries: healthcare, insurance, life sciences, aerospace, energy, manufacturing, financial services, and the United States government.

stories.headline: AI video startup Higgsfield in talks to raise up to $500M at a $5B pre-money valuation

key_facts.fact: The Information reported that AI video startup Higgsfield is in talks to raise $300 million to $500 million at a $5 billion pre-money valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: AI Video Startup in Talks to Quadruple Valuation to $5 Billion

key_facts.fact: The proposed valuation is more than four times the over $1.3 billion valuation Higgsfield reached in a January 2026 Series A extension.
key_facts.excerpt: This potential round would quadruple the company's valuation from January 2026, when it closed an extension to its Series A at over $1.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Higgsfield reportedly reached a $500 million annual revenue run rate by June 2026, up from $200 million in January, and counts over 15 million users with roughly 4.5 million daily video generations since its April 2025 launch.
key_facts.excerpt: The company achieved a $200 million annual revenue run rate (ARR) by January 2026... and further accelerated to $500 million ARR by June 2026... Higgsfield has accumulated over 15 million users since its public launch in April 2025, facilitating more than 4.5 million daily video generations.

key_facts.fact: Higgsfield was founded by Alex Mashrabov, former head of Generative AI at Snap, and integrates models such as Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, Veo 3 and Sora 2.
key_facts.excerpt: Higgsfield integrates advanced AI models such as Seedance 2.0, Kling 3.0, Veo 3, and Sora 2, offering features like Cinema Studio 3.5 for cinematic production and a Marketing Studio for URL-to-video ad generation.

stories.headline: Straiker raises $64M Series A to secure enterprise AI agents

key_facts.fact: Mountain View-based Straiker revealed on Monday, June 29 a $64 million Series A, bringing its total funding to $85 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Straiker, a startup building security software for enterprise AI agents, announced Monday that it has raised $64 million in a Series A funding round, bringing its total funding to $85 million.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Marathon Management Partners alongside Citi Ventures, Illuminate Ventures and Workday Ventures, with prior backers Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed; Marathon founding partner Gokul Rajaram joins the board.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series A round was led by Marathon Management Partners alongside Citi Ventures, Illuminate Ventures and Workday Ventures, with prior backers Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners LP also taking part. Gokul Rajaram, a founding partner at Marathon, is joining Straiker's board.

key_facts.fact: Straiker's platform discovers AI agents running inside an organization, tests them for weaknesses before deployment, and monitors their behavior at runtime; the company reports more than 15x run-rate revenue growth in under a year.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding comes as demand for AI agent security surges, with Straiker reporting 15x revenue growth in run rate in less than a year.

key_facts.fact: The raise rides surging agent adoption: IDC projects more than one billion AI agents deployed across enterprises by 2029, up from roughly 25 million in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Research firm IDC projects that more than one billion AI agents will be deployed across enterprises by 2029, up from roughly 25 million in 2025.

key_facts.fact: Straiker was founded in 2024 by Ankur Shah, ex-SVP and GM of Prisma Cloud at Palo Alto Networks, and Sreenath Kurupati, formerly of Akamai, and emerged publicly in March 2025 with $21 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Straiker emerged publicly in March 2025 with $21 million in initial funding.

stories.headline: AI leaderboard provider Arena hits $100M run-rate eight months after launching paid evals

key_facts.fact: Arena, the company behind the widely-cited Chatbot Arena leaderboard, reached $100 million in annualized run-rate revenue eight months after launching its paid AI Evaluations service in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Just eight months after launching its commercial service, AI leaderboard provider Arena, which originated as a research project at UC Berkeley in 2023, has reached $100 million in annualized run-rate revenue.

key_facts.fact: Revenue more than tripled from $30 million in January 2026, when Arena raised a $150 million Series A at a $1.7 billion post-money valuation; total funding raised stands at $250 million.
key_facts.excerpt: When the company raised a $150 million Series A at a $1.7 billion post-money valuation in January 2026, annualized revenue was $30 million. Several months on, that number has more than tripled, with $250 million raised in total.

key_facts.fact: CEO Anastasios Angelopoulos cautioned that the figure is consumption-based and not annualized recurring revenue in the classical sense, since customers pay for evaluations as they run them.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Anastasios Angelopoulos told TechCrunch the revenue is consumption-based, not annualized recurring revenue in the classical sense.

key_facts.fact: The paid AI Evaluations product sells deep-dive performance analytics drawn from a community that has submitted more than 10 million head-to-head model comparisons, putting Arena in competition with Scale AI, Surge and Mercor for post-training work.
key_facts.excerpt: Arena competes directly with Mercor, Surge, and Scale AI for AI post-training dollars while its free leaderboard continues attracting millions of users.
